newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria Capitalbank to hike capital to 2.2 bln lv.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria Capitalbank to hike capital to 2.2 bln lv.

text.p: Bulgaria's private Capitalbank plans to raise capital to 2.2 billion levs by the end of 1997 to meet central bank requirements for a full licence, the bank's board chairman said on Monday.

"The shareholders decided today to raise the bank's capital from current 500 million levs to 1.4 billion levs by March 31, 1997 and to 2.2 billion levs by the end of next year," Angel Parvanov told Reuters.
Under central bank minimum capital requirement Bulgarian commercial banks should have 1.4 billion levs for a domestic licence and 2.2 billion levs for a full one by the end of March next year.
Capitalbank's fully paid-in capital amounts to some 500 million levs after acquisition of 28 percent of the bank by two Russian companies.
Bulgaria's First Financial company, headed by Parvanov, is the main shareholder with 47 percent.
The remaining 25 percent is held by state-owned firm Teraton, which expects a government decision to transfer its stake to other investors.
